title: The Tunguska Event
hook: In 1908, a massive blast flattened a Siberian forest. No crater was found.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: Over Siberia, a fireball lit the sky before an enormous explosion.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: The blast flattened about eighty million trees across two thousand square kilometers.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: Yet investigators who reached the site years later found no impact crater at all.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: About sixty kilometres away, the shockwave threw a man from his chair.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: Scientists now think a small asteroid or comet exploded high in the atmosphere.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: It remains the largest impact event in recorded history, yet the object itself was never found.

end.line: So what really exploded over Siberia that day?

description: On 30 June 1908, a huge explosion flattened about 2,000 square kilometers of Siberian forest, yet no crater or fragments were ever found. Scientists believe it was an asteroid that exploded in mid-air.

facts.claim: On 30 June 1908, a massive explosion flattened about 80 million trees over roughly 2,000 square kilometers of Siberian forest near the Podkamennaya Tunguska River.
Eyewitnesses reported a bright fireball and a shockwave that knocked people off their feet many kilometers away.
The first scientific expedition did not reach the remote site until 1927, led by Leonid Kulik.
No impact crater or meteorite fragments were ever found at the site.
The leading scientific explanation is that a small asteroid or comet, roughly 50 to 60 meters across, exploded in an airburst several kilometers above the ground.
It remains the largest impact-related event in recorded history.
